tool: PATCHED dosbox-pure tracing core (tools/libretro/dosbox_pure_libretro.dylib, build-core.sh) driven by HostClient (packages/mcp/src/live/host-client.ts): drive a FRESH BOOT to the corridor (state 5), trace the relocated FUN_1c94 entry, capture-on-breakpoint the cs-relative selection tables + each per-tile descriptor segment. summary: RESOLVED the long-open #079 blocker: the tile-0 and tile-1 wall-texture atlases are extracted, eyeball-validated as real dithered stone textures, committed, and wired into the wall rasterizer's per-tile atlas selection. RESULT: maze-wall-cases-parity.test.ts lifts from 15/32 to 22/32 byte-exact gated cases (the 7 newly-gated cases are tile-0/1 front-walls/far-shapes: case-07/08/16/17/18/19/21, all 100.00% wall-region byte-exact). THE KEY RE: FUN_1c94 (ega.drv entry 10) selects its descriptor-table+atlas segment per call as descSeg = cs:[0x169] + cs:[0x17a + 2*tile], where cs:[0x169] is the atlas BASE segment (=0x4e0e in the corridor frame) and cs:[0x17a+2*tile] is the per-tile paragraph delta. For the corridor: tile0 desc seg = 0x4e0e, tile1 = 0x4f8e, tile2 = 0x514e (matching the prior tile-2 finding). THE STALENESS GOTCHA (the reason this was blocked): cs:[0x169]/cs:[0x17a] AND the descriptor segments themselves are VOLATILE in the relocated transient copy — an idle/settled read() returns stale/overwritten bytes (per maze-texture-decode.json source-region-decode-not-stone). Both the selection words and each tile segment are valid ONLY at a FUN_1c94 hit, so they must be CAPTURED ON BREAKPOINT (the patched core's capture-on-breakpoint armed at the FUN_1c94 entry). The patched core cannot unserialize the committed states (err unser, the documented maze-background-fromasset.json wall) — but it CAN drive a fresh boot into the corridor + trace, which is the path taken (no committed-state load needed). VALIDATIONS: (a) the captured tile-2 atlas is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the previously-committed tile-2 atlas (0 diffs across 0x4000 B; piece 0xb {srcPtr 0x1cd8,w4,h6}, piece 0xe {0x22d8,w4,h5} cross-check passes). (b) the captured tile-0/1/2 segments are byte-identical across two independent fresh-boot runs (reproducible, not heap noise). (c) tile-0 (7 pieces) and tile-1 (22 pieces, the 3x5/2x3/1x2 perspective front-wall sequence) decode (4-plane EGA cell format) to recognizable dithered stone wall textures (eyeballed via per-piece PNGs). NOTE: not all 8 tile slots are walls — tile 4 (seg 0x550e) decodes to readable TEXT ('DBASIC3'/'BORDENG' with a blue UI frame) = a shared font/UI heap, NOT a wall atlas; tiles 5/6 are empty. Only tiles 0/1/2 are wall atlases (and they are exactly the tiles the 32 C1 wall-cases draw).

findings.claim: FUN_1c94 (ega.drv entry 10, the wall/sprite compositor) resolves its per-call descriptor-table + source-atlas segment as descSeg = cs:[0x169] + cs:[0x17a + 2*tile], where tile = the call's [bp+0xc] arg (= span.walltype). cs:[0x169] = the atlas BASE segment; cs:[0x17a + 2*tile] = a per-tile paragraph (>>4 segment) delta. Captured at a FUN_1c94 hit on a fresh-boot corridor frame: cs:[0x169]=0x4e0e; tile deltas {0:0x0, 1:0x180, 2:0x340, 3:0x600, 4:0x700, ...} -> tile segs {0:0x4e0e, 1:0x4f8e, 2:0x514e, 3:0x540e, 4:0x550e, ...}. The tile-2 seg 0x514e matches docs/re/findings/maze-stage1-compositor.json (the corridor draws tile 2). The resolved ds (after FUN_1c94's `mov ds,bx`) for the 2 corridor wall pieces was 0x514e = tile 2, confirming the selection.

evidence.details: tools/libretro/probe-tile-atlas.ts (+ the integrated tools/parity/extract-maze-assets.ts): drive fresh boot to state 5, find the wmaze render sig (OVL 0x4784), trace the relocated FUN_1c94 entry (lin 0x6d6a4, cs=0x6b91, 11 hits), capture-on-breakpoint the cs segment window [cs<<4+0x160, +0x40) at the first hit -> read cs:[0x169]=0x4e0e + cs:[0x17a+2t]. The corridor's resolved ds per FUN_1c94 call (traced at AFTER_DS = entry + (0x1cc9-0x1c94)) = 0x514e 0x514e = tile 2. AN IDLE read() of (cs<<4)+0x169 returned the STALE value 0x1c0 (wrong) — confirming the volatility; the capture-at-hit value 0x4e0e is correct.

findings.claim: The per-tile descriptor segments (0x4e0e/0x4f8e/0x514e) hold valid descriptor-table + 4-plane source cells ONLY at a FUN_1c94 hit; a settled/idle read returns stale/overwritten bytes (the buffers are re-decoded per group, per maze-texture-decode.json). An idle read of tile-2 seg 0x514e in a redrawn-then-settled frame decoded to garbage (p1: src=0xf801,w=248,h=248), while a capture-on-breakpoint of the same seg at the FUN_1c94 hit gave the correct descriptor table (p1: src=0x258,w=7,h=6; piece 0xb {0x1cd8,4,6}). So the c2 blocker ('tile-0/1 atlas cannot be captured from settled states') is RESOLVED not by re-minting states under the patched core, but by capturing each tile segment ON BREAKPOINT during a fresh-boot corridor redraw — the tile-0/1 descriptor tables + atlases are fully resident at that instant regardless of which tile the current frame draws (the cs:[0x17a] table holds all tiles' segs).

findings.claim: The tile-0 and tile-1 pieces decode (the cracked 4-plane EGA 8x8 32-byte cell format — egadrv-blit-internals.json / maze-texture-decode.json) to recognizable DITHERED STONE WALL TEXTURES, not noise. tile-1 piece 1 (3x5 = 24x40px) = a stone-block column with vertical mortar lines + a transparent right margin (a perspective front-wall face); tile-1 holds the receding 3x5 -> 2x3 -> 1x2 perspective sequence (4 such triads). tile-0 piece 3 (7x7 = 56x56px) = a dense dithered near-wall block face. tile-2 piece 0xb (the known corridor wall face) = a regular brick/mortar grid (byte-identical to the prior committed atlas). The colors render as EGA-default magenta/cyan (color 13/3) because the Wiz6 palette remap (13->grey etc.) is applied downstream; the mortar/stone STRUCTURE is unambiguous. CAVEAT (NOT-walls): tile 4 (seg 0x550e) decodes to readable TEXT ('DBASIC3'/'BORDENG' in a blue UI frame) = a shared font/UI graphics heap; tiles 5/6 are empty. Only tiles 0/1/2 are wall atlases — and those are exactly the tiles the 32 C1 wall-cases draw (per maze-wall-cases-c2.json per_case_table).
